check.reason: The satirical headline and the take both say enforcement can wait 'until July.' The real headline only says enforcement is paused and gives no date, so the July deadline is an unsupported specific that may be invented. The headline also recasts a pause as the administration 'giving states until' a date 'to start removing people,' which changes what the story is about. The target (the administration and bureaucracy) and the tone are fine, and nothing mocks patients or quotes the article. To pass, drop the date or confirm it from the source, and keep the framing to a pause in enforcement.

pick.title: Trump Admin Pauses Enforcement of Its Medicaid Work Rules
pick.headline: Administration Gives States Until July to Start Removing People From Medicaid
pick.take: The work requirement is national and mandatory, except that enforcement can now wait until July. It's good to see the system grant itself the grace period it has never offered anyone with a missing form. Deadlines, it turns out, are flexible when the bureaucracy is the one racing them.
